title: Invited: Leveraging Machine Learning for Quantum Compilation Optimization
problem: NISQ devices require dynamic remapping of logical qubits to physical qubits during compilation to handle limited connectivity and qubit constraints. This qubit routing problem is NP-hard and current heuristic solutions add unnecessary gates, reducing algorithm fidelity.
motivation: Minimizing added gates in quantum routing is critical for preserving algorithm fidelity and reducing quantum resource overhead on near-term quantum processors.
method: The paper uses a machine learning model (a Seq2Seq Transformer, a neural network designed to learn patterns in instruction sequences) to predict optimal qubit routing. The model learns from examples of quantum gate operations and SWAP instructions—operations that rearrange which physical qubits represent which logical qubits to fit the processor's connectivity constraints—then predicts where each logical qubit should map onto the actual physical qubits of a quantum processor. Unlike routing strategies hand-written for each specific processor design, this learned approach works across different quantum hardware backends without requiring manual tuning.
key_novelty: Using a machine learning model (a Seq2Seq Transformer: a neural network that learns patterns in instruction sequences) to automatically discover qubit routing eliminates hand-written hardware-specific routing rules and enables one model to work across different quantum processor designs.
contributions: Seq2Seq Transformer-based approach to NP-hard qubit routing problem
Significant reduction in quantum gate overhead compared to heuristic search methods
Learning method that generalizes across different quantum backend configurations
Removal of manual heuristic design dependency for QPU-specific optimization

metrics.other: Reduced quantum computing resource overhead vs. heuristic search algorithms

limitations: Specific quantitative results and performance metrics not discussed in abstract.
